materials.text:
A carved pendant of black granite in the form of an Egyptian cat, approximately 2 inches (5 cm) in height, hung from a sturdy thong of plaited leather. Not only does the token guarantee the affection of any feline the owner encounters, but it also safeguards them against the attentions of cat-demons, who will not attack them, except in self-defense.
Should the wearer ever harm a cat, the amulet shatters, transforming into a cat-demon, which seeks vengeance on the perpetrator.

If they are wearing Bast’s cat amulets, Wu won’t harm the investigators (unless they attack first); the same cannot be said if they have not received Bast’s boon and attempt to interfere with the creature’s plans. Even if they are wearing the cat amulets, Wu doesn’t mind watching Lung harm them—just because it’s expected to be friendly towards them doesn’t mean it has to protect them from others.

A carved pendant of black granite in the form of an Egyptian cat, approximately 2 inches (5 cm) in height, hung from a sturdy thong of plaited leather. Not only does the token guarantee the affection of any feline the owner encounters, but it also safeguards them against the attentions of cat-demons, who will not attack them, except in self-defense.
Should the wearer ever harm a cat, the amulet shatters, transforming into a cat-demon, which seeks vengeance on the perpetrator.

The black-granite Egyptian-cat pendant grants its owner feline affection and keeps cat-demons from attacking, except when they defend themselves. If its wearer ever harms a cat, the amulet shatters and becomes a cat-demon seeking revenge on the person who harmed the cat.

A carved pendant of black granite in the form of an Egyptian cat, approximately 2 inches (5 cm) in height, hung from a sturdy thong of plaited leather. Not only does the token guarantee the affection of any feline the owner encounters, but it also safeguards them against the attentions of cat-demons, who will not attack them, except in self-defense.
Should the wearer ever harm a cat, the amulet shatters, transforming into a cat-demon, which seeks vengeance on the perpetrator.

If they are wearing Bast’s cat amulets, Wu won’t harm the investigators (unless they attack first); the same cannot be said if they have not received Bast’s boon and attempt to interfere with the creature’s plans. Even if they are wearing the cat amulets, Wu doesn’t mind watching Lung harm them—just because it’s expected to be friendly towards them doesn’t mean it has to protect them from others.

Keeper note: Bast’s Boon—if the investigators gained Bast’s favor through their actions during The Black Cat sidetrack scenario (page 326, Egypt), then they have a boon—their cat amulets (Appendix D: Artifacts, page 653). If they happen to be wearing the amulets when they visit Mr. Lung, the Siamese cat is incredibly friendly, rubbing itself around their legs and allowing them to pet it.

The black-granite Egyptian-cat pendant grants its owner feline affection and keeps cat-demons from attacking, except when they defend themselves. If its wearer ever harms a cat, the amulet shatters and becomes a cat-demon seeking revenge on the person who harmed the cat.

Wu will not harm investigators wearing Bast’s cat amulets unless they attack first. Investigators without Bast’s boon who interfere with its plans do not have that assurance. Even with the amulets on, Wu is willing to watch Lung hurt the investigators: being expected to act friendly does not oblige Wu to protect them from other people.
The notes discuss Bast’s cat pendant, feline affection, protective effects and their limitations, as well as Wu’s attitude toward the investigators.
